items.title: Tamil finfluencer Harish’s death exposes enforcement gap in regulating financial advisers
items.summary: The death of a 27-year-old Tamil financial influencer V Harish has triggered a polarising discussion on social media. The Chennai police have arrested YouTuber Jason Samuel on suicide abetment charges, and the case is currently under investigation. The tragic death has put a spotlight on India’s largely unregulated finfluencer (short for financial influencer) landscape. Harish, who ran the “Finance with Harish” account, had more than 1.3 million followers. He died by suicide on October 20, days after YouTuber Jason Samuel published a video questioning his credentials, alleging that he had offered securities-related advice without the required Stock and Exchanges Board of India (SEBI) registration. Harish’s Instagram account had also been suspended. Samuel alleged that Meta, the parent company of Instagram, acted after receiving reports about Harish’s alleged misleading content but the circumstances of the suspension have not been independently established. Harish’s family accused Jason, arrested on charges of abetting suicide, of harassment and extortion. The case has stirred a debate over whether online criticism crossed into cyberbullying. Jason has denied these allegations. Besi

items.title: Dharmasthala case explained: The latest findings and unanswered questions
items.summary: A lot has happened since we last spoke about the Dharmasthala case. And because we’ve been following this story closely and reporting on it through all these developments, I thought it was time we sat down and made sense of where things stand. Last year, the focus was on Chinnaiah - the masked man who came forward with massive claims about mass burials in and around Dharmasthala. But that story eventually fell apart. The state government constituted a Special Investigation Team, or SIT, to investigate his allegations. But instead of the hundreds of bodies that Chinnaiah had initially claimed he had buried, the excavations unearthed just two skeletons- both male. Chinnaiah subsequently changed his version. He was arrested, and the SIT initiated perjury proceedings against him. He has also alleged that he was forced by a few people to make these claims and they were also booked by the police. But now, there are new developments. The Karnataka State Women’s Commission has written to the state government asking for the SIT’s mandate to be expanded. Why? Besides these, Veeramani was also booked for the abetment of a minor’s suicide in 2004. According to the Greater Chennai Police, the latest POCSO case was registered on October 21, based on a complaint and statement from another minor girl. items.title: Hyderabad: BJP MP Eatala Rajender to lead march over Jawahar Nagar dumpyard pollution
items.summary: BJP MP from Telangana Eatala Rajender has called for an end to fresh garbage being brought to Hyderabad’s Jawahar Nagar dumpyard, and for the waste already accumulated there to be processed and recycled. The Malkajgiri MP said that the pollution from the site is causing serious health problems for people in nearby neighbourhoods including Yapral, Dammaiguda, Kapra, Alwal, among others. As part of a campaign against the dumpyard, the BJP leader has announced a march beginning October 27. Speaking at a roundtable meeting he organised on Sunday, October 25, Eatala Rajender called for waste-processing facilities with zero-pollution technology. He said waste could be converted into electricity, biogas and organic manure rather than dumped indiscriminately. He also said he would seek support and funding from the Union government in this regard. The MP said that pollution from the Jawahar Nagar dumpyard affects areas within a 25-to-30-kilometre radius and that residents face hazardous living conditions. items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. items.title: Youth protests across Europe: the overlapping crises facing Gen Z
items.summary: Young people are facing a future that feels increasingly uncertain. Although every generation experiences turbulence while navigating adolescence, the pressures experienced by Gen Z – those born between 1997 and 2012 – are different and seem more pervasive. From climate change and mental health concerns to academic pressure, housing costs, job and economic insecurity, today’s young people are navigating a complex set of expectations. Understanding their frustrations, including those expressed through protests across Europe, requires looking beyond individual experiences to the social conditions shaping their lives. Adolescence has long been seen as a period of “storm and stress”. This reflecting a belief that is a universal and inevitable period of emotional turmoil, behavioural conflict and identity crisis. However, this has been increasingly challenged. Rather than being defined solely by difficulty and disruption, adolescence is increasingly viewed as a period of possibility, opportunity and growth . items.title: Lula is declared winner of Brazil's election as Bolsonaro rejects results
items.summary: By Eléonore Hughes, Mauricio Savarese And Anna-catherine Brigida Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a vocal critic of U.S. President Donald Trump, was reelected Sunday in a result that provides relief to critics of widening U.S. influence in Latin America . With 100% of the vote counted, Brazil’s electoral court announced that the soon to be 81-year-old Lula had a lead of nearly 4.4 million votes over opponent Flávio Bolsonaro, giving him 51.8% of the total vote. Bolsonaro quickly refused to concede defeat and asked for the election results to be annulled after an evening of chaos at some polling places that followed a last-minute decision to extend voting by two hours. Bolsonaro is the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, whom Lula defeated to take the presidency in 2022. Lula's triumph bucks a regional trend of victories for right-of-center presidential candidates allied with Trump. It also means Latin America’s largest economy, with a GDP of $2.6 trillion per year, will likely continue defying Trump’s demands, despite the pressure of increased tariffs .
